explanation: After the coup the military cared more about political control and left economic policy to a group of technocrats under Delfim Netto. The model that followed rested on low wages, rising exports and inflows of foreign capital. A government answerable to voters would have found those three harder to hold together. James Petras’s reading, which Wikipedia carries, makes the seizure of power and the system of military-police control part of what the growth was built on. The edge is `enabled`. The regime did not produce ten per cent a year by decree, and it is what made that model available.
